habitat: Singly or in groups on seasonal pans, floodplains, dams, lagoons and rivers. It feeds by sweeping a partly open bill sideways under the water. It breeds colonially in reeds or trees and is nomadic when not breeding.
summary: A fairly common resident. A white waterbird with a spoon-shaped bill. The identification line says a red face, a red-and-grey bill and red legs. The description says a pink bill and pink legs. The immature has brown streaks on the wings and head. Newman does not describe the voice. The Kemp name African Spoonbill and the code VB were left unchanged.

bill.shape: Spatulate and spoon-shaped. The identification line says red and grey. The description says pink.

head.pattern: White, with a red face on the identification line. The description does not repeat the face colour.
Immature wings and head streaked brown.

viewNotes.note: Red face on the identification line. The bill is red and grey there, and pink in the description.
White. Flight pattern is not otherwise described.
The underside in flight is not described.

calls.description: Newman does not describe the voice. The grade A call is from Port Alfred. The filename is XC385073-African Spoonbill.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. It is nomadic when not breeding. The bill and legs are red on the identification line and pink in the description, so neither colour is stored. The grade A call is from the Eastern Cape. The iNaturalist account has no display name, so the login copper is credited. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^4=16 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 8–32.
